implemented_requirements.requirement: Computer selects a hidden sequence of colors (or digits)
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameEngine.__init__ calls self._generate_secret() which creates a list of random palette indices (see game_engine.py lines 19‑30).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player attempts to guess the hidden sequence within a set number of tries
implemented_requirements.evidence: play_round in main.py loops while not engine.is_over(), using engine.max_attempts and engine.attempts_used to enforce the limit (see main.py lines 45‑71).

implemented_requirements.requirement: After each guess, show feedback regarding correct color and correct position
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameEngine.evaluate_guess returns (exact, partial) and CLI.show_feedback prints "Result: {exact} exact ●, {partial} partial ○" (see cli.py lines 46‑55).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Distinguish between exact matches and partial color matches
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board._feedback_row builds a row with "●" for exact matches and "○" for partial matches (board.py lines 24‑30).
CLI.show_win and CLI.show_lose are called when engine.is_win() or when the loop ends without a win (see main.py lines 61‑73).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Render a history board of previous attempts
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class stores rows and renders a full board with guesses and feedback (board.py lines 9‑44).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Handle input robustness (quit, help, invalid input)
implemented_requirements.evidence: CLI._read_line converts EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt to QuitRoundError; CLI.prompt_guess handles 'quit' and 'help' commands (cli.py lines 12‑44).

critical_issues: A stray file gameengine.py contains an incomplete stub of GameEngine, but it is never imported, so it does not affect execution.
No explicit unit tests are provided, but the code appears logically sound.
judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable implementation of the classic Mastermind game. Core gameplay, secret generation, guess handling, exact/partial feedback, board rendering, and win/lose messages are all present and wired together in main.py. Minor concerns are limited to an unused stub file, which does not impact the functional program.
